title: Tap a beer keg with a Sankey D coupler
instruction: Tap the keg with the coupler.
context: Changing kegs is routine bar work: the coupler goes onto the keg's Sankey valve, turns a quarter turn under the valve's lugs, and only then is the handle pushed down, which drives the probe into the valve and opens it. Pressing the handle first pushes the probe into an unlocked coupler, which on a pressurised keg blows it off and sprays beer. Done by bartenders (O*NET 35-3011.00; 711,140 US jobs in BLS OEWS May 2023), who change kegs on shift, and barbacks (35-9011.00, dining room and cafeteria attendants and bartender helpers, 483,390).
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left); heights above the counter top. Keg: a sixtel (26 kg) of which only the top is modelled, standing free on the counter centred at x 28, y 0: a 23 cm stainless 12-sided top plate 1.2 cm up, a 4 mm chime ring round its edge 4 cm tall, and in the middle the Sankey D valve neck, a 3.4 cm octagon rising 1.6 cm above the plate (top 2.8 cm up) with two dark bayonet lugs on its left and right faces. Drip tray: fixed black block 10 x 10 x 0.8 cm at x 28, y -20. Coupler: chrome Sankey D coupler, 0.9 kg in all, standing on the tray: a 6.4 cm square base with a 6 mm skirt (5.6 cm inside) that fits over the valve neck, orange bayonet ears on its left and right, a 4.6 cm square body 4.6 cm tall, a black beer outlet 1.6 cm square on top (2.5 cm tall) with an elbow turned down its far (+x) face, and a dark gas inlet on that face below it. Its handle (8 cm chrome bar with a black grip, 100 g) is pivoted on the body's near side 4.4 cm above the base, pointing toward the robot, raised 35 deg; it turns down 60 deg to a stop, on a spring that holds it up until the bar passes horizontal (over centre) and holds it down after. Inside, a probe (50 g) is cammed by the handle 11.5 mm down into the valve. Lines: both stay connected all episode. Beer line: 36 cm of 1 cm clear vinyl from the outlet elbow (4.6 cm up), looping round the far side of the tray (out to y -26) to the shank of a fixed chrome tap tower (4 x 4 x 28 cm) at x 43, y -7. Gas line: 36 cm of 1.2 cm red hose from the inlet (3 cm up), on a similar loop out to y -25 (1.6 cm lower), to a fixed blue CO2 regulator (yellow shutoff lever on top) at x 49, y -5. Each is twelve 3 cm segments of 20 g on spring joints (bend sideways, bend up/down, twist; 0.01 N m/rad each); each end fitting is welded to its fixture and lets go above 60 N. Their weight and stiffness act on the coupler while it is carried, seated and turned. The bayonet lugs hold the coupler where it is turned and draw it to the stop over the last 15 deg.
scoring: From the episode's recorded poses (the trial video on a real rig). Caught: the coupler set on the valve neck within 5 mm of its axis, upright within 5 deg, ears within 10 deg of the lugs; it then turns only about the valve, clockwise seen from above, to a stop at 90 deg. Score 0, latched for the episode, if the handle is pushed more than 30 deg down while the coupler is turned less than 80 deg, if the keg moves more than 10 mm or tilts more than 5 deg, if the coupler is knocked over (tilted more than 30 deg) or put down on the bare counter, or if the beer or gas line is pulled more than 5 mm off its fitting; also 0 if the coupler never caught. Otherwise the sum of: caught 0.1; turned 85 deg or more 0.25; handle locked over centre (52 deg or more down) 0.35; probe 90% or more of its travel into the valve 0.2; turned 85 deg or more, with no gripper within 2 cm of the coupler or handle and both still, for 1 s 0.1. Success at 1.0 held 1 s. Scored at the last step.
reset_notes: Lift the handle back up past centre, turn the coupler back 90 deg and lift it off the valve, stand it on the drip tray with the handle pointing at the robot and both lines lying in their loops, check both line fittings are tight, and set the keg on its outline with the lugs left and right.
fidelity: Rigid boxes, one friction. Keg cut to its top 4 cm, 26 kg. Bayonet is a joint: catches when seated within 5 mm/10 deg, turns 0-90 deg, holds where left. Handle over-centre and probe are springs. Lines: chains of rigid 3 cm segments on soft spring joints, ends welded (break 60 N). No beer or CO2: on a rig use an empty keg shell ballasted to 26 kg, lines connected, regulator shutoff closed (0 psi).
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; demo: 1.0 (two runs); no-turn degenerate demo: 0.0
